g.text: Short Polling vs. Long Polling vs. WebSocket
Same 10-second span, three different request/connection shapes
7 requests in 10s, 6 of them wasted -- latency on the 6th poll's update is up to ~1.7s
3 round trips in 10s instead of 7, near-immediate delivery -- but each hold ties up a server-side connection the whole time
single upgraded TCP connection stays open, full-duplex
messages flow either direction at any moment -- no request has to precede a response
Round trips for the same 10s window: short polling 7, long polling 3, WebSocket 0 (one connection, not a request).
Server-side cost shifts the other way: short polling holds nothing between polls; long polling holds one connection per
waiting client for the hold duration; a WebSocket holds one connection per client for as long as they're connected, period.
That's why WebSocket load balancing has to be sticky -- see load-balancing.md -- while stateless HTTP polling never needed to care.
